title: Setup And Defaults
intro: Install setup before document annotations. Configuration can precede it. Reapply setup after replacing a native page foreground/background; identities and counters persist.

entries.summary: Document show rule: installs registration, references, visibility, validation and optional page overlays.
entries.note: Set page geometry/layers first. Page footnotes default to native flow; override-page-footnotes: true makes the foreground overlay their default. Host themes may install both overlay hooks with page-overlays: false.

entries.summary: Host integration hook for one page overlay; does not initialize the annotation registry.
entries.note: Install background too: it records page geometry. See the setup guide for host-owned/scoped composition.

entries.summary: Updates subsequent defaults in the current Deixis scope; ordinary Typst brackets do not create a settings scope.
entries.note: Top-level auto leaves settings unchanged. Type/component maps merge compatible branches; empty maps and branch auto have option-specific reset semantics. All accepted setting names are listed in the shared-options section. omit: (series: ("todo",)) removes selected annotations while preserving passages; none includes all series. `deixis-configure` is an identical alias; `short.configure` uses the same function.

entries.summary: Opt-in module of short aliases. Use configure for settings and note-block for Deixis scopes; native block remains available.
entries.note: Use short as dx for qualified calls. All function aliases preserve identity; configure replaces the keyword set and note-block preserves native block. See the getting-started guide for import syntax.

title: Marks And Identity
intro: Use id to create the original counter owner; of reuses it. Names accept nonempty strings or labels. An original, its one body and reused marks may appear in any order. Reuse does not add a drawn connector.

entries.summary: Unified original/reused mark. Defaults to inline; pins select region mode. A call without id/of is anonymous decoration.
entries.note: mark-type: "region" highlights a passage or pins; "phantom" is a semantic origin. Set data on creation, not reuse. See shared options for styles, targets and region controls.

entries.summary: Specialized inline form of deixis-mark, with an optional marked passage.
entries.note: Box, highlight, underline, parentheses, text-fill and none are available. Reused marks retain the original styles beneath explicit overrides.

entries.summary: Highlights a passage or a pin-defined region, with page-local fragment geometry.
entries.note: Supply passage or pins, never both. A flow region must fit one page. Foreground/background regions may span pages. Region marker numerals remain foreground.

entries.summary: Creates/reuses an invisible semantic original; its body may still carry a numbered marker.
entries.note: Phantom reuse accepts no passage or appearance overrides. An anonymous phantom draws nothing and consumes no palette slot.

title: Bodies And Collections
intro: Wrappers accept [body] or [passage][body]. A -body call takes [body]. Wrapper id creates original + body; -body id creates a standalone body. With of, both forms attach only a body. Margin, inset and endnote bodies capture declaration typography; page footnotes use the native footer.

entries.summary: Allocates a native footer slot at the body declaration, even when its original mark is on another page.
entries.note: Native flow (the default) paginates long bodies and uses the footer's typography; separator/gap are native footnote.entry settings. Overlay footnotes reserve space but paint whole units. Local block footnotes collect at the block end. numbering: (restart: "page", pattern: "1") restarts displayed markers on each original page; assigned counts stay stable.

entries.summary: Overlay bodies follow the original mark or anchor pin; native margin packing may spill onto later existing pages.
entries.note: Leave a wide page margin. Flow places exactly on the declaration page with no collision packing. overflow: "error" checks the final frame. Connector shorthand selects the original mark.

entries.summary: Margin-note presets for the outside margin and loose mark alignment.
entries.note: Uses margin-note configuration/query type. Explicit arguments override the preset; mark-align-strictness: auto resumes configured strictness.

entries.summary: Review-comment preset: a margin note in the "review" series with lettered markers, author/status data and a bold header.
entries.note: Omit the series for a final copy with deixis-set(omit: (series: ("review",))). Other options are margin-note options; of is rejected.

entries.summary: Callout whose page defaults to its body declaration; use anchors, offsets or a placement callback for deliberate positioning.
entries.note: Flow is the factory body layer. Overlay declarations are invisible in flow. The connector layer is independent. Custom containers receive container-args.

entries.summary: An explanation in native flow: the wrapper places it right after its passage as an inline aside; a -body call places it where called.
entries.note: The wrapper defaults to inline: true and keeps the sentence; inline: false gives a callout after the line (the -body default). Inline decoration bypasses block containers/custom single renderers. breakable: false supplies one frame for an explicit body endpoint.

entries.summary: Declares a collected explanation, rendered only by an eligible endnote printer.
entries.note: Wrapper series defaults to "endnote"; attachments inherit the original series. The printer controls where it appears. Body settings are retained until printing.

entries.summary: Prints unprinted eligible bodies in source order; successive printers do not duplicate output.
entries.note: Omitted overrides retain body settings. Default grid bypasses single-note containers; select deixis-native-render-group to use them. after/before are exclusive source boundaries.

title: Connections And Drawing
intro: A body connector is the short path for margin/inset notes. Independent edges select document endpoints without creating or moving them. Connections paint in their own foreground/background layer, below bodies at matching priorities.

entries.summary: Draws an independent edge between marks, bodies, attached objects or pins; declarations may precede endpoints.
entries.note: Bare from IDs select original marks; bare to IDs select bodies. Use (mark: id, occurrence: name), (body: id, point: "end"), (node: id) or (pin: target) explicitly. Default route is straight, or sharp orthogonal inside deixis-routing.

entries.summary: Show-rule wrapper that captures a policy for individual connections and enabled margin/inset shorthand.
entries.note: manual keeps native routes; avoid searches independently; separate adds bounded group repair. Search needs sharp orthogonal geometry. Registered objects stay fixed. Nested wrappers form separate groups.

entries.summary: Builds source-local line/cubic geometry from finite absolute coordinates, optionally using a prepared scene.
entries.note: Coordinates use x-right/y-down. origin is the source; segments are relative to it. No measurement or painting. Scene routes can fail: inspect status/detail before preparation. Avoidance requires sharp orthogonal paths.

entries.summary: Prepares reusable fixed rectangles/points in caller-defined page planes.
entries.note: Numeric nodes need no setup. Selectors for document marks/bodies/pins need setup + context. Node behavior is avoid, ignore, cut or cross; the latter two do not add visual indicators.

entries.summary: Plans up to sixteen explicit sharp orthogonal page fragments together against a prepared scene.
entries.note: Result routes retain input order. quality has before/after metrics; stats reports bounded work. No registration or painting. Complete separation/global optimality is not guaranteed. Preparing a document-derived scene still needs setup.

entries.summary: Prepares existing geometry for native/custom paint without repeating routing. Head callbacks run here.
entries.note: Place the painted request at path.origin yourself. Relative styles/custom heads may need context. It consults no document defaults, page layer or automatic crossing group.

entries.summary: Paints a prepared connector request, including shafts, heads and optional decorations.
entries.note: Numeric painting adds no layout dimensions; reserve the drawing area and place at the source origin. In document callbacks this is the default-painter delegation helper.

entries.summary: Constructs a reusable head specification; stealth is a filled triangular head with an open notch.
entries.note: Other native shapes include triangle, vee, circle, diamond and bar. Custom render(request) returns body, trim and bounds in a tip-local +x frame. Omitted dimensions scale with the shaft. Disable endpoint heads with heads: none.

entries.summary: Paints a prepared head in its local frame. A missing head or zero direction emits nothing.
entries.note: Use prepared heads from the connector request, not the raw specification returned by deixis-arrowhead.

title: Pins And Attachments
intro: Pin names and attachment IDs accept string/label spellings. They have independent namespaces from note IDs. A pin is a point; an attached routing object registers one live, nonbreaking frame.

entries.summary: Publishes a geometric anchor at its declaration; padding expands bounds around that anchor.
entries.note: Default "text" padding follows local text metrics. Percentages have no pin-size basis. Scope namespaces pins independently of note/block identities.

entries.summary: Wraps rendered content to attach pins, scan marked tokens, or register a selectable routing node.
entries.note: id registers a routing frame with avoid behavior by default. Generated node ports are the four side midpoints. pins can define custom outlets. Explicit avoid/ignore/cut/cross also registers anonymous nodes. Pin-only attachments keep their native breakability.

title: Scopes And Counters
intro: Scope names and note IDs are independent. Blocks own rendering instances and counter streams; thread shares a rendering domain, while counter synchronization only shares numbering.

entries.summary: Creates local annotation rendering/settings/counter scope around native content.
entries.note: Minipage maps margin to internal inset and fixes outset at 0pt. Named IDs are unique; automatic scopes stay private. Breakable blocks use per-page margin frames and collect local footnotes at the block end.

entries.summary: Reads the assigned counter value for a scope and literal series. Use inside context.
entries.note: Unused streams start at zero. This is not a total annotation count. Page numbering resets do not reset note counters. Opt-in page-local display markers do not change this assigned value.

entries.summary: Sets a stream to an integer or applies current → integer. The next original increments that value.
entries.note: Bodies, references and reuse never increment. Earlier notes keep assigned numbers. Endnote wrappers use the "endnote" series; select it explicitly for their resets.

title: References And Custom Views
intro: Queries return safe semantic records and summaries instead of replaying live annotation content. An annotation remains one entry even when several marks share its body.

entries.summary: References one or more annotations, retaining original marker styling and native fallback for ordinary labels.
entries.note: @detail uses the native bridge installed by setup. Repeated reference targets deduplicate; compatible numeric ranges can collapse. Explicit marker-style overrides formatting.

entries.summary: One safe structured record per selected annotation. Page queries follow native body order; the unfiltered catalogue follows source order. Call inside context.
entries.note: Page queries include standalone bodies and require complete unique live spans. order: "source" / "body" and include-unpaired override automatic defaults. Each record retains all shared marks, safe summaries and optional body metadata; no live body content is returned.

entries.summary: Ready-made linked list over the annotation catalogue; custom callbacks can replace summaries or presentation.
entries.note: One entry per annotation, with links to all marked pages. Use query-notes for cards/tables or occurrence indexes. data can supply a custom title/status.

entries.summary: Shows repeated content with its marked passages but without creating marks, bodies or connections again.
entries.note: Native outlines apply it to heading and caption entries automatically. Use it for running headers and custom tables of contents that repeat annotated headings.

title: Rendering Extension Points
intro: These hooks consume supplied records or content; they do not create a registered annotation. When used in live document annotations, keep setup active and preserve destination/content helpers. Relative typography and backlinks may require context.

entries.summary: Built-in single-body layouts. Native keeps a natural text flow; aligned accepts a shared marker column.
entries.note: Use supplied data unchanged when delegating. Aligned additionally accepts max-marker-width/max-marker-gap. The container and body-style come from the body record.

entries.summary: Stack bodies, align stacked markers, or lay markers/content directly in two grid columns.
entries.note: Native/aligned groups delegate to each single renderer. Grid bypasses single renderers and containers. Empty groups produce no content. Supplied records may contain live document behavior.

entries.summary: Composable helpers for a custom body renderer: one destination, a marker, live content span, and return links.
entries.note: Emit meta OR marker once; marker already includes meta. Content publishes start/end spans and preserves nested palette ownership. Measurement records suppress live metadata. Backlinks read document origins and need setup/context.

entries.summary: Body wrappers: identity, native rect alias, or a left-bar alert. Container arguments are forwarded separately from shared styles.
entries.note: container-func accepts names plain, rect, alert, stripe and tinted, or a custom function. The first three select these existing exports; stripe and tinted are named-only accent presets. Explicit stroke/fill/radius and container-args override preset defaults. rect-container has native rect parameters. Alert doubles scalar border thickness on the left; native edge maps remain literal.

entries.summary: Region-shape callbacks for rectangular or elliptical bounds.
entries.note: Shape records provide width, height, fill/stroke and rectangle radius. Region registration/fragment selection belongs to the calling mark, not these painters. Use region marks with stroke: none for a highlight; add region-shape: deixis-ellipse-region for an ellipse.

title: Low-Level Layout Hooks
intro: Advanced hooks use supplied measured records and geometry. Most documents should choose note adapters, container/render callbacks, or routing APIs instead. Native layout and document lookup are separate responsibilities.

entries.summary: Numeric margin adapter hooks: exact ignores collisions; adaptive packs; flow distributes available space.
entries.note: All share min-margin-width, pushed-notes and extra arguments. Supply accepted page geometry and prepared notes. They paint locally through the layout adapter. These hooks are not the body layer: "flow" switch.

entries.summary: Immediate placement relative to selected pin bounds on the call's page.
entries.note: Pin lookup reads document geometry. Native placement can disturb flow.

entries.summary: Immediate placement in physical page coordinates, ignoring margins.
entries.note: Accepts content, or alignment + content; dx/dy default to 0pt. Fixed page dimensions need no setup. An auto page axis needs setup-provided page frames for accepted dimensions. This is placement, not dimension reservation.
